answer: AI agent economies resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to solve unique reasoning challenges every epoch—problems that demand fresh inference, not cached answers. An attacker spinning up fake agents hits a cost marble: every duplicate must burn compute to pass. Like inspectors at a wharf checking cargo manifests that change daily, the network sets horizon-shifting puzzles—logic games, novel proofs—that scale linearly with fake count, making mass impersonation prohibitively expensive while honest agents pay once.
